Insight1.summary: In aged female and male mice, senescence and DAM gene expression was more pronounced in fimbria-fornix and corpus callosum white matter than in hippocampal gray matter. Age-dependent increases in these transcriptional signatures were observed more consistently in white matter than in the hippocampus or cerebellum, emphasizing white matter susceptibility to late-life senescence and DAM changes.
Insight1.how: The authors compared RT-PCR measurements from microdissected fimbria-fornix and corpus callosum white matter with hippocampal gray matter in aged female and male mice. Several senescence and DAM-related genes were significantly higher in white matter, with additional female- or male-specific changes among particular transcripts. Comparisons with young, sex-matched mice showed that some genes increased in both gray and white matter, whereas a broader set increased in aged white matter, and the regional heat map showed more consistent age-related increases in white matter than in hippocampus or cerebellum. These findings support regional susceptibility of white matter to late-life transcriptional changes, but do not by themselves establish a mechanistically selective vulnerability.
Insight1.relevant: We investigated senescence and microglial gene expression patterns in microdissected fimbria-fornix and corpus callosum white matter relative to hippocampal gray matter of aged female and male mice (Fig. 1). p16ink4a (Fig. 1a), Cdkn2a (Fig. 1b), Lgals3 (Fig. 1c), Cdkn1a/p21 (Fig. 1d) and Ccl2 (Fig. 1e) expression were significantly higher in fimbria-fornix and corpus callosum compared with hippocampus. In aged female mice, Ccl5 (Fig. 1f), Apoe (Fig. 1g) and Gpr34 (Fig. 1h) expression were significantly higher in fimbria-fornix and corpus callosum compared with hippocampus. Relative to young counterparts, p16ink4a, Cdkn2a, Csf1r, Gpr34 and Trem2 expression increased in both gray and white matter microdissections of old male and female mice (Fig. 1i,j). Apoe, Bcl2a1a, Cd11b, Klk8, Lgals3, Cdkn1a/p21 and Tmem173 expression increased in old female and male fimbria-fornix and corpus callosum. Ccl2, Ccl5, Il1b and Tyrobp increased in old male fimbria-fornix and corpus callosum (Fig. 1j). In aged female and male mice, senescence and DAM gene expression was more pronounced in white matter relative to hippocampal gray matter. At the regional level, we observed age-dependent increases in genes such as p16ink4a, Cdkn2a, Lgals3, Apoe, Bcl2a1a, Cd11b, Csf1r, Klk8, Tmem173, Trem2 and Tyrobp more consistently in old fimbria-fornix and corpus callosum (Fig. 1k) than in the hippocampus or cerebellum, emphasizing that white matter is susceptible to late-life changes in senescence and DAM transcriptional signatures.

Which conclusion is best supported by these cross-regional measurements?

options.A: Aged white matter shows more pronounced senescence and pro-inflammatory gene expression than aged hippocampal gray matter, because the same set of transcripts was significantly elevated in fimbria-fornix and corpus callosum relative to hippocampus within the same aged animals.
options.B: Aged hippocampal gray matter is transcriptionally more inflamed than white matter, because the measurements only sampled aged mice and the white-matter elevations could reflect baseline regional differences.
options.C: These genes are specific markers of white-matter aging and not expressed in gray matter, because every measured transcript was significantly higher in fimbria-fornix and corpus callosum than in hippocampus.
options.D: The white-matter elevations prove that microglia in fimbria-fornix and corpus callosum are the unique cellular source of the measured transcripts, because these genes are known DAM and senescence markers.

rubric.correct_reasoning: The cross-regional comparison within the same aged animals shows p16ink4a, Cdkn2a, Lgals3, Cdkn1a/p21, and Ccl2 were each significantly higher in fimbria-fornix and corpus callosum than in hippocampus. The conclusion is that aged white matter exhibits more pronounced senescence and pro-inflammatory transcriptional signatures than aged hippocampal gray matter, and the reasoning correctly ties this to the within-animal, across-region direction of the differences.

distractor_analysis.B: Wrong conclusion (inverts direction). The reasoning attempts to dismiss the white-matter elevation by appealing to a missing young control, but the stated evidence already establishes that these transcripts were significantly higher in white matter than hippocampus within the aged cohort.
distractor_analysis.C: Wrong conclusion (overclaims exclusivity). A higher expression in white matter does not mean the genes are absent in gray matter; the data only show relative elevation, and the genes were detected (measured) in hippocampal tissue as part of the comparison.
distractor_analysis.D: Wrong conclusion (overclaims cellular attribution). The measurements are bulk tissue RT-PCR from microdissected regions, not isolated microglia, so they cannot localize the transcripts to microglia, let alone uniquely to white-matter microglia.

options.B: White matter is selectively vulnerable to late-life senescence and DAM transcriptional changes, because the white-matter regions showed more age-related transcripts and a broader age-induced gene set than hippocampus or cerebellum.
options.A: Hippocampus and cerebellum are protected from aging-related transcriptional changes, because fewer transcripts increased with age in those regions than in fimbria-fornix and corpus callosum.
options.C: Male mice age differently from female mice in every white-matter region, because Ccl2, Ccl5, Il1b, and Tyrobp increased only in old male fimbria-fornix and corpus callosum.
options.D: The brain shows a uniform aging transcriptional signature across all regions, because some genes (p16ink4a, Cdkn2a, Csf1r, Gpr34, Trem2) increased in both gray and white matter.

rubric.correct_reasoning: Two premises must be chained: (1) more age-dependent transcripts increased in fimbria-fornix and corpus callosum than in hippocampus or cerebellum, and (2) a broader age-induced gene set appeared in white matter. Together these support the conclusion that white matter is selectively susceptible to late-life senescence/DAM transcriptional changes, without overclaiming a proven mechanistic gate.

distractor_analysis.A: Wrong conclusion. 'Fewer transcripts increased' is consistent with a smaller or different age response, not with full protection; the evidence does not establish that hippocampus/cerebellum are immune to aging changes.
distractor_analysis.C: Wrong conclusion (overclaims). Four transcripts increasing only in males shows sex-specific additions in male white matter, not that every white-matter region differs between sexes.
distractor_analysis.D: Wrong conclusion. A shared subset of genes rising in both gray and white matter does not imply uniformity, since an additional, broader set rose in white matter only — the opposite of a uniform signature.

Insight2.summary: GAL3+ cells are rare in young mouse brains but accumulate densely in aged white matter tracts, especially the fimbria, where GAL3 colocalizes with IBA1 rather than GFAP. In aged female fimbria, IBA1+GAL3+ cells are larger than IBA1+GAL3− cells and show higher or trending-higher levels of uPAR and CD38; the age-associated increase in GAL3 area is more pronounced in females, while dPP4 elevation was demonstrated only for fimbria myeloid cells overall.
Insight2.how: Immunofluorescence mapped GAL3 in young and aged brains and used IBA1 and GFAP costaining to establish its association with myeloid rather than astrocytic cells in the fimbria. Sex-stratified measurements showed greater GAL3-positive area in old versus young female fimbria, whereas the corresponding male comparison was not significant. Morphological analysis found that IBA1+GAL3+ cells were larger than IBA1+GAL3− cells in old female fimbria, and PCA distinguished populations associated with GAL3 immunoreactivity. Imaging mass cytometry further showed that aged fimbria myeloid cells had greater GAL3, CD38, uPAR, dPP4, IBA1, and CD45 intensity than hippocampal myeloid cells, while the GAL3-stratified analysis specifically supported enrichment of uPAR and CD38, not dPP4.
Insight2.relevant: GAL3+ cells were rare in young mouse brains. In aged brains, we observed GAL3+ cells in multiple limbic regions (Extended Data Fig. 1a) with dense localization in white matter tracts, especially the fimbria (Extended Data Fig. 1a). In aged fimbria, GAL3 signal colocalized with the myeloid/microglial marker IBA1 but not with the astrocyte marker GFAP (Extended Data Fig. 1b,c). GAL3 immunoreactivity comprised a larger area of old versus young female fimbria; however, GAL3 area was not significantly different in fimbria between old and young male mice (Extended Data Fig. 1d). In the old female fimbria, IBA1+GAL3+ cells were larger relative to IBA1+GAL3− cells (Extended Data Fig. 1e,f). PCA of IBA1+GAL3+ and IBA1+GAL3− populations from old mouse fimbria revealed size-specific principal components based on cellular morphology and distinguished by GAL3+ immunoreactivity (Extended Data Fig. 1g). Thus, immunofluorescent imaging and gene expression demonstrate increased abundance of the senescent and DAM marker GAL3/Lgals3 in aged white matter, including the fimbria, which was more pronounced in aged female mice. […] Fimbria myeloid cells exhibited greater intensity of IBA1, GAL3, CD38, uPAR, dPP4 and CD45, relative to hippocampal myeloid cells, which exhibited greater CX3CR1 protein levels (Fig. 2b). Stratification of GAL3+ and GAL3− cells in the fimbria showed that GAL3+ cells harbored trending or significantly higher levels of senescence-related markers uPAR and CD38 (Fig. 2c).

GAL3+ area is significantly greater in old vs. young female fimbria, but not significantly different between old and young male fimbria. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.A: GAL3 marks a myeloid population that expands preferentially in aged female white matter, because colocalization with IBA1 (not GFAP) localizes the signal to microglia/myeloid cells and the sex-stratified increase was detected in females but not males.
options.C: GAL3 is primarily an astrocyte marker in the aged fimbria, because the dense white-matter signal could reflect astrocytic reactivity even though GFAP costaining was negative.
options.B: GAL3 accumulation in white matter is sex-independent, because the analysis considered male and female fimbria together across age.
options.D: GAL3 marks a neuronal population in the aged fimbria, because white matter tracts contain axons and the IBA1 costaining could reflect phagocytosis rather than lineage identity.

distractor_analysis.A: Holds the wrong conclusion (astrocyte identity), overriding the negative GFAP costaining; a single-premise reading focused on white-matter density without weighing the costaining controls.
distractor_analysis.B: Asserts sex independence by appealing to a pooled-analysis reading, but the stem explicitly reports a female-specific significant increase and a non-significant male comparison, so the sex dependence is the stated finding.
distractor_analysis.D: Invokes a neuronal/phagocytic alternative to dismiss the IBA1 colocalization; the stem treats IBA1 as the myeloid/microglial marker whose overlap with GAL3 establishes lineage, not phagocytic artifact.

options.B: dPP4 elevation in fimbria myeloid cells indicates dPP4 is independent of GAL3 status, because stratification by GAL3 showed no differential dPP4 expression.
options.C: uPAR and CD38 are elevated in all fimbria myeloid cells regardless of GAL3, because the overall fimbria comparison showed higher intensity of these markers.

distractor_analysis.A: Right marker but wrong specificity — the stem specifies that dPP4 elevation was shown for fimbria myeloid cells overall, not specifically in GAL3+ cells, so attributing dPP4 to the GAL3+ subset overreads the stratification result.

Insight3.summary: GeoMx digital spatial profiling of aged female mouse brains found that established senescence- and DAM-associated genes (Fth1, Ctss, and Apoe) and candidate or emergent genes (Ccno and Sesn3) were enriched in fimbria IBA1+ microglia relative to hippocampal IBA1+ populations. Within the aged fimbria, Apoe was the most abundantly expressed transcript in IBA1+GAL3+ relative to IBA1+GAL3− microglia and strongly distinguished these populations.
Insight3.how: The authors used GeoMx whole-transcriptome spatial profiling on 5-µm FFPE sagittal sections from 28-month-old female mouse brains, selecting areas with IBA1, GAL3, and SYTO83 and using GFAP for negative selection. They compared IBA1+ populations from hippocampus and fimbria and found enrichment of Fth1, Ctss, Apoe, Ccno, and Sesn3 in fimbria IBA1+ cells. They also compared IBA1+GAL3+ and IBA1+GAL3− populations within the aged fimbria, where Apoe was the most abundantly expressed gene in the GAL3+ population relative to the GAL3− population. Differential expression was analyzed with a two-sided DESeq2 Wald test, and the authors cautioned that GeoMx DSP is useful for signature discovery but limited for molecularly phenotyping rare or heterogeneous cell populations.
Insight3.relevant: We next examined microglial transcriptional signatures specific to the hippocampus and fimbria of old female mice using GeoMx DSP. We segmented the hippocampus and fimbria regions with positive selection based on GAL3, IBA1 and SYTO83 labels and negative selection by GFAP (Fig. 3a). First, we compared IBA1+ populations in the hippocampus versus fimbria (Fig. 3b). Established senescence and DAM genes Fth1, Ctss and Apoe and candidate senescence-related genes, Ccno and Sesn3, were enriched in IBA1+ cells of the fimbria. We next compared transcriptional profiles of IBA1+GAL3+ and IBA1+GAL3− microglia specifically in aged fimbria (Fig. 3c,d). Apoe was the most abundantly expressed gene in IBA1+GAL3+ cells, relative to IBA1+GAL3− cells. We discovered conserved senescence- and DAM-associated genes (Fth1, Apoe and Ctss) and emergent genes (Ccno and Sesn3) were enriched in aged fimbria microglia. Apoe strongly distinguished GAL3+ versus GAL3− microglia in the fimbria. These experiments underscore the utility of GeoMx for expression signature discovery; however, GeoMx DSP remains limited for molecularly phenotyping rare or heterogenous cell populations.

mcq_questions.question: In 28-month-old female mouse brain sections, GeoMx DSP segmented fimbria and hippocampus using positive selection for IBA1, GAL3, and SYTO83 with GFAP-based negative selection. When IBA1+ populations from the fimbria were compared with IBA1+ populations from the hippocampus, Fth1, Ctss, Apoe, Ccno, and Sesn3 were each enriched in fimbria IBA1+ cells. Apoe was also the most abundantly expressed transcript in IBA1+GAL3+ versus IBA1+GAL3− microglia within the aged fimbria. Which conclusion is best supported by these observations?

options.B: Apoe is enriched in fimbria IBA1+ cells relative to hippocampal IBA1+ cells because it is the most abundant transcript in IBA1+GAL3+ microglia of the fimbria, indicating a shared regional and GAL3-defined program.
options.C: Apoe, Fth1, Ctss, Ccno, and Sesn3 are enriched in fimbria IBA1+ cells relative to hippocampal IBA1+ cells because the GeoMx segmentation used GFAP to exclude astrocytes, showing the signal is microglial.
options.A: The set of genes enriched in fimbria IBA1+ cells relative to hippocampal IBA1+ cells includes established senescence/DAM genes (Fth1, Ctss, Apoe) and candidate genes (Ccno, Sesn3), and within the fimbria Apoe also most strongly distinguishes IBA1+GAL3+ from IBA1+GAL3− microglia.
options.D: Apoe is the most abundant transcript in IBA1+GAL3+ microglia of the aged fimbria because GeoMx DSP captures single-cell transcriptomes, and this abundance proves GAL3+ cells are the source of the Apoe enrichment seen between fimbria and hippocampus.

rubric.correct_reasoning: Option C correctly states both observations given in the stem: (1) the cross-regional comparison identified Fth1, Ctss, Apoe (established senescence/DAM) plus Ccno and Sesn3 (candidate/emergent) as enriched in fimbria IBA1+ versus hippocampal IBA1+ cells, and (2) within the fimbria Apoe was the most abundant transcript distinguishing IBA1+GAL3+ from IBA1+GAL3− microglia. The reasoning combines the two stated comparisons without overinterpreting mechanism.

distractor_analysis.B: Wrong reasoning. Apoe being most abundant in IBA1+GAL3+ cells does not establish that the same mechanism explains the fimbria-versus-hippocampus enrichment; these are two separate comparisons (regional and GAL3 status), and conflating them misreads the design.
distractor_analysis.C: Wrong reasoning. GFAP-based negative selection removes astrocytes but does not by itself demonstrate that the enriched genes are microglial in origin; the genes could come from other non-astrocyte, non-GFAP-selected cells in the segment. The conclusion that 'the signal is microglial' overstates what the selection strategy proves.
distractor_analysis.D: Wrong conclusion and reasoning. GeoMx DSP is not single-cell; it profiles segmented regions containing many cells. Apoe abundance in the GAL3+ comparison does not prove GAL3+ cells are the source of the fimbria-vs-hippocampus enrichment, and the authors explicitly note DSP limitations for phenotyping heterogeneous populations.

mcq_questions.question: GeoMx DSP of 28-month-old female mouse brain used IBA1/GAL3/SYTO83 segmentation with GFAP exclusion to compare IBA1+ cells across regions and across GAL3 status within the fimbria. Five genes (Fth1, Ctss, Apoe, Ccno, Sesn3) were enriched in fimbria versus hippocampal IBA1+ cells, and Apoe was the top differential transcript between IBA1+GAL3+ and IBA1+GAL3− microglia within the fimbria. Given these observations, what does the evidence most directly license?

options.A: The five enriched genes define a senescence/DAM program that is uniformly expressed by every IBA1+ microglia in the aged fimbria, because they were detected above background in the fimbria IBA1+ segment.
options.B: Apoe marks the IBA1+GAL3+ subset within the aged fimbria while Fth1, Ctss, Ccno, and Sesn3 show regional (fimbria-vs-hippocampus) enrichment in IBA1+ cells, so the cross-regional and GAL3-status comparisons identify overlapping but non-identical gene sets.
options.C: GAL3 expression in IBA1+ cells of the aged fimbria is the cause of the fimbria-versus-hippocampus enrichment of Fth1, Ctss, Apoe, Ccno, and Sesn3, because Apoe was the top gene distinguishing IBA1+GAL3+ from IBA1+GAL3− cells.
options.D: The fimbria-versus-hippocampus enrichment of the five genes and the IBA1+GAL3+ versus IBA1+GAL3− enrichment of Apoe are equivalent findings, because both comparisons used DESeq2 and the same IBA1+ segmentation strategy.

rubric.correct_reasoning: Option B integrates the two comparisons: the regional comparison (fimbria IBA1+ vs hippocampal IBA1+) identified five genes including Fth1, Ctss, Apoe, Ccno, and Sesn3 as enriched, while the within-fimbria GAL3-status comparison specifically highlighted Apoe. These are overlapping but distinct gene sets — Apoe appears in both, but Fth1, Ctss, Ccno, and Sesn3 are not stated as the top differentiators of the GAL3+ vs GAL3− contrast. This combination of premises matches what the data show.

distractor_analysis.A: Wrong conclusion. Detection of the five genes above background in a segmented IBA1+ region does not establish that every IBA1+ microglia in the fimbria uniformly expresses them; segment-level averages cannot resolve cell-to-cell uniformity, and the authors explicitly caution that DSP is limited for phenotyping heterogeneous populations.
distractor_analysis.C: Wrong conclusion and reasoning. Observing Apoe as the top gene distinguishing GAL3+ from GAL3− cells within the fimbria does not establish that GAL3 expression is the cause of the regional enrichment, which was defined across all IBA1+ cells of the fimbria versus hippocampus regardless of GAL3 status.
distractor_analysis.D: Wrong conclusion. The two comparisons differ in their grouping variable (region vs GAL3 status) and in their reported top hits (five genes vs Apoe), so they are not equivalent findings even though they share methodology. Equating them ignores what each contrast actually measured.

Insight5.summary: Senescence transcriptional programs in aged white-matter microglia are integrated within the broader DAM continuum rather than constituting a separable microglial state. The aged-only white matter-enriched cluster 7 shows enrichment across all six SenBrain domains, while the age-exclusive cluster 10 in the young-versus-old comparison is selectively enriched for SASP, organelle stress, and cell surface domains, with nuclear stress specifically marking the distinct age-dominant cluster 3. Organelle stress and cell surface domains are shared across aged populations, and SenBrain enrichment is inversely related to homeostatic microglial identity.
Insight5.how: The SenBrain panel was parsed into six senescence domains and scored per cell using AddModuleScore. In dataset 1 (aged microglia), white matter-enriched cluster 7 demonstrated pronounced enrichment across all six senescence domains (Fig. 4m). In dataset 2 (young vs. old), the age-exclusive cluster 10 showed the highest overall SenBrain score but was specifically enriched for cell surface, organelle stress, and SASP domains, while age-dominant cluster 3 showed nuclear stress enrichment (Fig. 6d). SenBrain scores showed an inverse relationship with homeostatic microglial module enrichment (Figs. 5j, 6b,c; Extended Data Fig. 3c,d). Cross-dataset harmonization confirmed a conserved senescent-DAM population (Extended Data Fig. 7j). The authors conclude that at these ages, senescence programs appear integrated with the DAM signature rather than forming a discrete subset, and that distinct senescent DAM subsets may only resolve at older ages or in neurodegenerative models.
Insight5.relevant: We parsed the SenBrain panel into senescence domains (Supplementary Table 2) and investigated the scores and percentage of cells enriched for individual modules. The white matter-enriched cluster 7 demonstrated pronounced frequency and expression enrichment across all investigated senescence domains, including cell cycle regulation, nuclear stress, SASP, senescent cell anti-apoptotic pathway (SCAP), organelle stress and cell surface markers (Fig. 4m). This corresponded to comparatively elevated expression of specific senescence-related genes, including Cdkn2d/p19ink4d (cell cycle regulation); Cenpb, Hmgb1, Pak2 and Smad2 (nuclear stress); Ccl3–4, Csf1, Mmp12 and Spp1 (SASP); Akt1 and Bcl2l1 (SCAP); Cyba, Lgals3, Lgals3bp and Lpl (organelle stress); and Axl, Cd9, Gpnmb and Plaur (cell surface markers) (Fig. 4g). … Age-exclusive cluster 10 was enriched for senescence domains including cell surface, organelle stress and SASP, implicating this population as a dominant proinflammatory microglial phenotype (Fig. 6d). Age-dominant cluster 3 was enriched for cell surface, organelle stress and nuclear stress domains (Fig. 6d). … Organelle stress and cell surface remodeling emerged as shared senescence domains, whereas SASP and nuclear stress domains were distinctly enriched among the two age-increased populations. … For several clusters, SenBrain enrichment was inversely related to the homeostatic-associated microglia module (Figs. 5j and 6b,c and Extended Data Fig. 3c,d). … In our analysis of 24- and 4-month-old female mice, senescence-associated transcriptional programs appear integrated with the broader DAM signature. Insight6.summary: Canonical senescence biomarkers are detected only sparsely and heterogeneously in aged microglia—Cdkn2a/p16 was found in just 1–5% of cells with a heterogeneous profile, and the age-exclusive senescent-DAM cluster showed only low Cdkn2c/p18ink4c—leading the authors to caution that no single marker defines senescence and that multi-biomarker, multi-domain scoring is required.
Insight6.how: Within the CosMx datasets, the authors examined all microglia expressing any Cdkn and compared them to Cdkn-negative microglia, and separately interrogated the Cdkn2a+ fraction across age groups (Extended Data Fig. 6a–d). Microglia expressing any Cdkn showed increased Cdkn1b, Cdkn2a, Cdkn2c, Apoe, Csf3r, Hmgb1, Tgfbr1, Cyfip1, P2ry12 and Sparc; aged versus young Cdkn2a+ microglia differed in Cdkn2a, Apoe, C1qa and Clu (up) and Trem2 and Serpine1 (down), indicating age-dependent functional divergence. Methodologically, the CosMx probes for Cdkn2a span both p16ink4a and p19arf exons, and the platform lacks signal amplification, limiting detection of low-abundance transcripts; the authors state that additional approaches are needed to conclusively map p16-positive microglial identity. The SenBrain panel description explicitly advises analysts to require a minimum of two to three distinct biomarkers and/or senescence domains, acknowledging that any individual SenBrain gene may be altered in non-senescent contexts. The authors also note that Cdkn2c/p18ink4c, which can coordinate cell-cycle arrest via CDK4/CDK6, was lowly detected even in the cluster 10 senescent DAM population.
Insight6.relevant: Among all aged microglia, we observed that the expression profiles across distinct and total Cdkn+ microglia were heterogenous (Supplementary Fig. 2). Furthermore, we detected low-level expression of multiple Cdkns across most individual microglial populations; cluster 8 harbored the highest expression (Extended Data Fig. 2j). […] Examination of the cell cycle regulation domain revealed that young and old microglia broadly and lowly expressed cell cycle regulatory markers (Extended Data Fig. 6). In examination of microglia expressing any Cdkn, the genes Cdkn1b, Cdkn2a, Cdkn2c, Apoe, Csf3r, Hmgb1, Tgfbr1, Cyfip1, P2ry12 and Sparc were increased relative to microglia without Cdkn expression (Extended Data Fig. 6a). Across all microglial clusters, 1–5% of cells were positive for Cdkn2a. Among total aged versus young Cdkn2a+ microglia, we observed age-increased expression of Cdkn2a, Apoe, C1qa and Clu, and age-decreased expression of Trem2 and Serpine1, among other factors, suggesting distinct roles for Cdkn2a+ microglia in the aged versus young brain (Extended Data Fig. 6b). options.A: Cdkn2a marks a single, well-defined senescent microglial population because the percentage of positive cells is uniformly low across all clusters, indicating a consistent identity.
options.C: Cdkn2a is an unreliable senescence indicator in this dataset because the low detection rate, the heterogeneity of the Cdkn2a+ cells, and the lack of signal amplification together mean that p16-positive microglia cannot be conclusively mapped from these data alone.
options.B: Cdkn2a is the most reliable senescence marker because it was detected at low levels uniformly across clusters, demonstrating that every microglial cluster undergoes equivalent senescence.
options.D: Cdkn2a is not useful as a senescence marker because the heterogeneous expression profile shows it is co-expressed only with Apoe and C1qa, ruling out any link to microglial aging.

rubric.correct_reasoning: Keyed option C is correct because it combines three stated premises: (1) only 1–5% of microglia are Cdkn2a+, (2) the Cdkn2a+ fraction is heterogeneous across clusters, and (3) the CosMx Cdkn2a probe lacks signal amplification. Together these premises justify the conclusion that the data cannot conclusively map p16-positive microglial identity, which is exactly the authors' stated caveat. The combination of low abundance plus a probe that does not amplify means detection is limited, so a negative or sparse result cannot be taken as evidence of absence or homogeneity.

distractor_analysis.A: Wrong conclusion and wrong reasoning. The conclusion that Cdkn2a marks a single, well-defined population contradicts the stated heterogeneity, and the reasoning that a uniformly low percentage implies consistent identity inverts what low-plus-heterogeneous actually means.
distractor_analysis.B: Wrong conclusion and wrong reasoning. distractor_analysis.D: Wrong conclusion. The stated heterogeneity shows co-variation of Cdkn2a with several genes (Apoe, C1qa, Clu, Trem2, Serpine1), not only Apoe and C1qa, so the reasoning misrepresents the data and the conclusion overgeneralises from limited co-expression.

Insight7.summary: The authors converted a recognized technical artifact of spatial transcriptomics — low-level 'molecular shadow' transcripts misassigned from neighboring cells — into an analytical asset they termed molecular 'contact-tracing.' They showed that white matter-localized microglia carry spillover oligodendrocyte/myelin transcripts (Mbp, Mobp, Plp1) while gray matter-localized microglia carry neuronal spillover (Camk2a, Adcy1, Sncb, Snap25), with astrocytic markers partitioning as Aldoc (gray) versus Gfap (white); they formalized this into canonical cell-type gene-set modules that independently corroborated their anatomical cluster assignments.
Insight7.how: The authors first performed two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum differential expression between white matter- and gray matter-localized microglia (Fig. 4e), revealing region-specific enrichment of non-microglial markers interpreted as spillover from adjacent cells. They then constructed 'contact-tracing' gene-set modules for major brain cell types from published datasets (Supplementary Table 2) and scored each CosMx microglial cluster (Fig. 4j,k; Fig. 5j; Supplementary Fig. 5). In the young-versus-old dataset, clusters 2, 3, 9, 10 and 15 scored high on the oligodendrocyte module and localized to white matter; clusters 4, 7 and 14 scored high on the neuronal module and localized to gray matter; cluster 15 additionally scored on an ependymocyte module; cluster 1 scored on the microglial/homeostatic module; and cluster 13 showed enrichment for both the homeostatic and DAM modules, consistent with a transitional state. The same logic applied to non-microglial immune cells showed aged cells carrying elevated Gfap, Plp1, Mbp, Mobp and complement transcripts relative to young cells, interpreted as proximity to resident glia. The approach was confirmed with anatomical registration.
Insight7.relevant: "An inherent artifact of current single-cell spatial platforms and segmentation algorithms is low-level detection of transcripts from adjacent or interacting cells. By exploiting this signal as a variant of molecular 'contact-tracing', we observed that white matter-localized microglia were enriched for oligodendrocyte transcripts Mbp, Mobp and Plp1, whereas gray matter-localized microglia were distinctly enriched for neuronal transcripts Camk2a, Adcy1, Sncb and Snap25, indicating close proximity to, or potentially prior engulfment of these cells (Fig. 4e). Distinct astrocytic markers were enriched in gray (for example, Aldoc) and white (for example, Gfap) matter-localized microglia (Fig. 4e)." "To profile transcripts from neighboring and/or interacting cells, we devised canonical gene set modules of distinct brain cell types (Supplementary Table 2) using previously published data and interrogated the 'contact-tracing modules' and enrichment for SenBrain and DAM signatures in clusters (Fig. 4j–k). We detected enrichment for immune cell and choroid plexus related gene modules in cluster 1, 7 and 9, oligodendrocyte module in clusters 1 and 4, neuronal module in cluster 3 and astrocyte and vascular modules in cluster 9 (Fig. 4k)." "Microglial clusters 2, 3, 9, 10 and 15 exhibited higher oligodendrocyte module scores, whereas clusters 4, 7 and 14 exhibited higher neuron module scores, corroborating the white and gray matter-majority anatomical localizations (Fig. 5j, Extended Data Fig. 4c–i and Supplementary Fig. 5a). Clusters 1 and 13 were enriched for the microglia cell-type module, suggestive of homeostatic populations, whereas clusters 3, 10 and 13 were enriched for the DAM module… Cluster 15 was enriched for an ependymocyte module, suggesting proximity to ventricular borders (Fig. 5j and Supplementary Fig. 5d)." "Relative to young immune cells, higher levels of astrocyte (Gfap), oligodendrocyte (Plp1, Mbp and Mobp), and microglia (C1qa, C1qb and Ctss) markers were detected in old immune cells, suggesting proximity to brain-resident glia (Supplementary Fig. 3d)." "Current spatial mapping molecular markers and segmentation algorithms are imperfect, resulting in detection of 'molecular shadows', corresponding to low-level transcript localizations of cell identity markers that probably originate from adjacent cells rather than the segmented cell. We exploited this methodological artifact as a way of classifying spatial neighborhood characteristics of cell populations, which were confirmed with anatomical registration."

mcq_questions.question: In a spatial transcriptomics dataset of brain tissue, a researcher observes that white matter-localized microglial cells carry elevated levels of Mbp, Mobp and Plp1, while gray matter-localized microglial cells carry elevated Camk2a, Adcy1, Sncb and Snap25, with astrocyte markers splitting as Aldoc (gray) versus Gfap (white). Given that these transcripts are characteristic of other brain cell types rather than microglia, which interpretation is best supported?

options.B: Microglia in white matter have genuinely adopted an oligodendrocyte-like transcriptional program because the same transcripts (Mbp, Mobp, Plp1) are detected only there, indicating true lineage reprogramming of those microglia.
options.C: Microglia in gray matter are neuronal cells misclassified as microglia because they express Camk2a and Snap25, which are bona fide neuronal markers and should override the microglial assignment.
options.A: The region-specific non-microglial transcripts most likely reflect spillover from neighboring cells (oligodendrocytes in white matter, neurons in gray matter), so they encode each microglial cluster's spatial neighborhood rather than its true identity.
options.D: Aldoc and Gfap are microglial activation markers, and their partitioning by region shows that white matter microglia are activated while gray matter microglia are resting.

rubric.correct_reasoning: The observations describe low-level detection in microglia of transcripts (Mbp/Mobp/Plp1, Camk2a/Adcy1/Sncb/Snap25, Aldoc, Gfap) that are well-known markers of oligodendrocytes, neurons, and astrocytes respectively. Because these are markers of other cell types, the only interpretation supported is that they originate from adjacent cells and leak into the microglial segmentation. The regional concordance (oligodendrocyte markers in white matter, neuronal markers in gray matter, Gfap in white matter, Aldoc in gray matter) maps exactly onto the expected spatial distribution of those neighboring cells, which is what licenses the spillover/contact-tracing interpretation.

distractor_analysis.B: The conclusion that microglia have converted into oligodendrocyte-like cells is wrong; the reasoning confuses spillover with true expression. Just because Mbp/Mobp/Plp1 appear in white-matter microglia does not mean those microglia transcribe them — it means oligodendrocyte transcripts from nearby cells are being captured at low level in the microglial segmentation.
distractor_analysis.C: The conclusion that gray-matter cells are misclassified neurons is wrong. Camk2a and Snap25 in those cells are explained by spatial spillover from neighboring neurons; the microglial identity assignment does not get invalidated by the presence of a few low-level neuronal transcripts that are characteristic artifacts of the platform.
distractor_analysis.D: The conclusion that Aldoc/Gfap are microglial activation markers is wrong; the reasoning misreads canonical astrocyte markers as activation markers. The regional partition simply reflects the predominance of Gfap-high white-matter astrocytes versus Aldoc-high gray-matter astrocytes as the neighboring source.

mcq_questions.question: A researcher constructs cell-type 'contact-tracing' gene-set modules (oligodendrocyte, neuronal, astrocyte, vascular, ependymocyte, immune) from published data and scores each microglial spatial cluster. options.A: The module scores are biologically meaningless because they were built from published datasets and applied to a different platform.
options.C: Module scores cannot be used to validate anatomical localization because cluster identity must be confirmed by other means.
options.B: The module scores reproduce the spatial neighborhood of each cluster and also reveal age-associated increases in glial proximity in immune cells, supporting that low-level spillover transcripts are a reproducible, neighborhood-encoded signal across cell types and ages.

rubric.correct_reasoning: Two premises must be combined. distractor_analysis.A: The conclusion that the scores are meaningless is wrong; the reasoning rejects cross-platform use a priori, but the data actually show the modules recover the expected regional pattern in microglia and the expected glial proximity in aged immune cells, which is positive validation.
distractor_analysis.C: The conclusion that the scores cannot validate localization is wrong; the reasoning ignores that the modules independently recover the same white-versus-gray matter assignment that anatomical registration confirmed. They are therefore a valid localization marker, not just a cluster-identity marker.
distractor_analysis.D: The conclusion that aged immune cells have genuinely transdifferentiated into oligodendrocytes is wrong; the reasoning confuses low-level spillover with true expression. Mbp and Plp1 are detected because of proximity to oligodendrocytes, not because immune cells have switched lineage.

Insight8.summary: Monocle3 trajectory inference on the combined young-plus-old CosMx dataset suggests that the age-exclusive senescent-DAM population (cluster 10) can be reached by at least two anatomically distinct routes — a longer homeostatic gray-matter trajectory (1 → 13 → 3 → 10) and a more direct white-matter/ependymocyte–oligodendrocyte trajectory (8 → 15 → 3 → 10) — supporting the interpretation that microenvironmental priming, rather than a unique cellular origin, confers the convergent age-selective transcriptional signature.
Insight8.how: The authors first identified gradient increases in senescence/DAM marker expression and cell-percentage enrichment across clusters 1 → 13 → 3 → 10 (Fig. 6e). They applied Monocle3 to the integrated young+old CosMx microglia, excluding peripheral clusters unreachable from the core partition (Fig. 6f). A forward model rooted at homeostatic cluster 1 branched from cluster 3 into 9, 10, or 15 → 8 (Fig. 6g(i)); a retrograde model rooted at cluster 10 showed three precursor branches converging on it via cluster 15/8, cluster 9, and cluster 13 → 1 (Fig. 6g(ii)). The 8 → 15 → 3 → 10 route required the fewest branch points. Pseudotime distance from cluster 10 inversely correlated with SenBrain and DAM module scores. The authors interpret these convergent trajectories — alongside three non-exclusive biological scenarios — as evidence that anatomical microenvironmental context, rather than a singular lineage, shapes the common senescent-DAM transcriptional endpoint, while noting that spatially resolved lineage mapping is needed to validate these inferences.
Insight8.relevant: We next modeled fate trajectories that may give rise to age-increased microglial populations within the aged (n = 4) versus young (n = 4) dataset (Figs. 5 and 6). We examined SenBrain gene expression gradients that may indicate a trajectory from homeostatic microglia (cluster 1) toward the age-exclusive cluster 10 (Fig. 6e). Across clusters 1, 13, 3 and 10, we observed gradient increases in the percentage of cells and average expression for several senescence and DAM-associated markers, including Apoe, Axl, C4bi, Cd9, Clec7a, Ctsb, Lgals3 and Tyrobp. We applied Monocle3 trajectory inference, excluding peripheral clusters (2, 6, 11 and 12, as defined by the UMAP) that were unreachable from the main core partition (Fig. 6f). Our initial model included homeostatic cluster 1 as the pseudotime root and proceeded to cluster 13, following to 3, which then branched into 9, 10 or 15 → 8 terminal populations (Fig. 6g(i)). This 1 → 13 → 3 → 10 trajectory tracked with the age-increased transcript gradients described above (Fig. 6e) and was characterized by proportional decreases in young cell abundance (Fig. 5e(ii)). To explore alternative trajectories resulting in the age-increased populations, we interrogated a retrograde model with terminal cluster 10 as the pseudotime root (Fig. 6g(ii)). Inferred retrograde trajectories branched from cluster 10 to 3, bearing both DAM and SenBrain-enriched genes, then branched toward three trajectories: (1) ependymocyte-, astrocyte- and oligodendrocyte-associated cluster 15 and astrocyte-associated cluster 8, (2) choroid plexus and oligodendrocyte-associated cluster 9 and (3) DAM- and homeostatic-microglia-associated cluster 13 with continued branching toward neuron-associated populations, including homeostatic cluster 1 (Fig. 6g(ii)). Based on trajectory branching of subpopulations, we determined that the retrograde-inferred astrocyte-, ependymocyte- and oligodendrocyte-associated microglial trajectory involving population 15 (8 → 15 → 3 → 10) was the most direct route to cluster 10 and involved the fewest branch points, whereas the gray matter-enriched homeostatic microglial trajectory (1 → 13 → 3 → 10) contained more branch points (Fig. 6g(ii)). Pseudotime values were inversely correlated with SenBrain and DAM module scores, and the greatest pseudotime distance from cluster 10 was represented in terminal gray matter populations (Supplementary Fig. 6). The models suggest that senescent DAM cells may emerge along multiple possible molecular trajectories, probably resultant of anatomically defined microenvironment priming that ultimately confers common age-selective transcriptional signatures. Additional spatially resolved lineage mapping and cell–cell communication analyses are needed to validate lineage inferences and the context-dependent signaling networks that drive cell fate trajectories in brain aging and disease.

Insight9.summary: Systemic senescent-cell targeting partially reduced age-increased senescence and DAM gene expression in aged female white matter: pharmacogenetic ablation of p16+ cells with AP20187 lowered p16ink4a in female fimbria-fornix/corpus callosum and hippocampus and lowered Trem2, Tmem173 and Tyrobp in white matter, while both AP20187 and the BCL2-inhibitor venetoclax lowered Lgals3 in aged female FFCC — with venetoclax not reducing p16ink4a, consistent with the authors' interpretation that p16 and BCL2 targeting engage partially distinct molecular axes; male transcriptional responses were more heterogeneous.
Insight9.how: Old (16–20 month) p16-InkAttac mice were randomized by weight and age to vehicle, AP20187 (2 mg/kg i.p., which induces death of p16-expressing cells) or venetoclax (50 mg/kg oral gavage), on a regimen of five consecutive daily doses, 2 weeks off, then a second 5-day course, discontinued 1 week before necropsy; young vehicle-treated mice served as baseline. RT-PCR on microdissected FFCC and HIP was normalized to Hprt and to sex-matched young controls, and groups were compared by one-way ANOVA with exact P values versus old control (Fig. 7a–f). Sample sizes: n = 5/sex young control, n = 6F/8M old control, n = 4–5F/8M old AP20187, n = 5F/6M old venetoclax. In females, AP20187 reduced FFCC-p16ink4a (P = 0.0234), HIP-p16ink4a (P < 0.0001), FFCC-Trem2 (P = 0.0024), FFCC-Tmem173 (P = 0.0164) and FFCC-Tyrobp (P = 0.0256); AP20187 and venetoclax both reduced FFCC-Lgals3 (P = 0.0074 and P = 0.0160), but only AP20187 reduced p16ink4a. The authors note that transcriptional profiles were more heterogeneous in male mice and that larger validation cohorts are needed.

Insight10.summary: Senotherapeutics partially reverted the aged fimbria microglial phenotype toward a youthful state at cellular and tissue-architectural levels — reducing IBA1+ density and cell size, restoring youth-like alignment of microglia to fiber tracts, and lowering GAL3+ and APOE+ burden — with AP20187 and venetoclax converging on GAL3+ microglia through distinct effector routes (AP20187 reducing per-cell GAL3 intensity; venetoclax reducing IBA1+GAL3+ cell number without altering residual intensity). The authors posit that the fimbria's anatomical adjacency to the choroid plexus and lateral ventricle underlies both its selective age-related vulnerability and its responsiveness to systemic senotherapy, while cautioning that the same regimens alter young fimbria microglia, limiting translational application in young organisms.
Insight10.how: Using the opposite hemisphere from the gene-expression cohort (Fig. 7), the authors quantified IBA1+ immunofluorescence in young and old vehicle-, AP20187- and venetoclax-treated p16-InkAttac female fimbria (Fig. 8a–e). IBA1+ density was higher in old than young fimbria and was returned to youthful levels by AP20187 (P = 0.0095); both drugs reduced IBA1+ cell size (P = 0.0045, P = 0.0003) (Fig. 8b,c). Microglial alignment to DAPI-estimated fiber tracts (long-axis angular offset of each IBA1+ cell's Feret axis to the nearest tract) showed greater alignment in old versus young mice, and AP20187 shifted the distribution toward youth-like organization (Kolmogorov–Smirnov P < 0.001 for both comparisons) (Fig. 8d). A published microglial phenotyping composite index (cell area, convex hull area/density, perimeters, span ratio, Feret length, tract-angle offset, circularity) plus PCA separated old control microglia from young, old AP20187 and old venetoclax, with AP20187 cells shifting toward young profiles and venetoclax cells clustering by increased circularity and decreased size (Fig. 8e). Both drugs reduced GAL3 footprint and the frequency of IBA1+GAL3+ cells (Fig. 8f,g); AP20187 additionally lowered per-cell GAL3 intensity in remaining GAL3+ cells (KS P < 0.001), whereas venetoclax reduced cell number without altering residual intensity — interpreted as "distinct effector populations… converge on GAL3+ microglia" (Fig. 8h; Extended Data Fig. 8d,e). APOE immunofluorescence intensity and APOE/GAL3 colocalization were reduced by both drugs (Fig. 8i–l), and treated mice showed more dispersed APOE+ cell organization relative to the fimbria midline (Fig. 8m; Extended Data Fig. 9). The authors caution that the same regimens altered young fimbria microglia (venetoclax reduced IBA1+ abundance; both drugs increased cell size and reduced density), corresponding to low Cdkn2a and Bcl2 detection in young brain, limiting senolytic application in young organisms. They further posit that the fimbria's spatial adjunction to choroid plexus and lateral ventricle exposes it to circulating factors and infiltrating immune cells, potentially explaining both its aging vulnerability and its responsiveness to systemic senotherapy.
Insight10.relevant: "We next explored how senotherapeutics modulate aged white matter microglial identity, frequency, morphology and distribution. Using the opposite hemisphere of brains applied to gene expression profiling (Fig. 7), we conducted IBA1+ immunofluorescent imaging of microglia in young and old vehicle-treated, old AP20187-treated and old venetoclax-treated p16-InkAttac female fimbria (Fig. 8). Fimbria IBA1+ cells frequently exhibited spindle- or ameboid-like morphologies (Fig. 8a and Extended Data Fig. 8a,b). We observed greater abundance of IBA1+ cells in old versus young fimbria (Fig. 8a,b), and old IBA1+ cells exhibited larger cell areas (Fig. 8c). AP20187 treatment in old mice reduced IBA1+ cell density in the fimbria to youthful levels (Fig. 8b). AP20187 or venetoclax treatment decreased IBA1+ cell size, compared with old controls (Fig. 8c). We explored microglia organization to fiber tract architecture by analyzing the long-axis angular offset of each IBA1+ cell to the nearest neuronal fiber tract (Fig. 8d(i)). Microglia from old mice displayed greater alignment to fiber tracts than young controls, and AP20187 treatment shifted angular offset of microglia toward youth-like organization (Fig. 8d(ii)). […] These findings suggest that morphological properties of aged microglial populations in fimbria are partially reverted by senotherapeutic interventions." "Accordingly, we tested whether senotherapeutics alter age-increased IBA1+GAL3+ signals (Fig. 8a,f,h). AP20187 or venetoclax reduced the area and frequency of IBA1+GAL3+ cells in aged female fimbria (Fig. 8f,g)… GAL3 fluorescence intensity of remaining IBA1+GAL3+ cells from AP20187-treated female mice was lower compared with old controls (Fig. 8h). Although venetoclax decreased Lgals3 transcript (Fig. 7c) and reduced the total number of IBA1+GAL3+ cells in white matter (Fig. 8g), we did not detect differences in GAL3 fluorescence intensity of remaining IBA1+GAL3+ cells (Extended Data Fig. 8d,e). This collectively suggests distinct effector populations in venetoclax-mediated BCL2 versus AP20187-mediated p16 targeting converge on GAL3+ microglia." "Old control mice had significantly greater APOE immunofluorescence intensity than young mice, and AP20187 and venetoclax both reduced APOE signal (Fig. 8j and Extended Data Fig. 9b). AP20187 also reduced the percentage of APOE cells colocalized with IBA1 (Fig. 8k). Both senotherapeutics reduced the percentage of APOE+ cells colocalized with GAL3 (Fig. 8l). […] AP20187- or venetoclax-treated mice exhibited more dispersed APOE+ cell organization characterized by trends of decreased distance from the midline, relative to old control mice (Fig. 8i,m and Extended Data Fig. 9c–f). Collectively, the senotherapeutics reverted microglial morphological and molecular properties in the aged fimbria to more youthful states." "It is also likely that senotherapeutics target other senescent brain and peripheral cell types, which could impact microglia through local or circulatory interactions. Related to this notion, the fimbria is spatially adjoined by choroid plexus and the lateral ventricle, heightening its exposure to systemic circulating factors and infiltrating immune cells. We posit that the anatomical location of the fimbria may underlie both its vulnerability in aging and its responsiveness to senotherapeutic intervention." "Young fimbria microglia were mildly responsive to both drugs, which corresponded to low detection of Cdkn2a and Bcl2 in the young brain and emphasizing that senolytics can have effects that limit their application in young organisms."
